page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, configured with an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16), and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the c3d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% of tested instances. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth for small cached blocks fall into the average range. A notable bottleneck is observed in uncached memory operations, where both read and write bandwidth for large blocks are weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Similarly, while small-scale LLM inference (135M model) yields average processing speeds, medium-scale LLM inference (7B model) results in poor text generation throughput at 5.95 tokens per second.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, providing dedicated compute resources without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Given its average multi-core performance and weak uncached memory bandwidth, it is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and basic text or image processing, rather than memory-intensive analytics or large-scale machine learning inference.
